title: statistically-driven-exposure-controller-and-autorestore-for-model-upgrades
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem statement: Teams deploying new model versions lack a single, reproducible way to define experiments that automatically control exposure by statistical signal and restore traffic when regressions are detected. Current canary flows are ad-hoc: manual ramping, separate monitoring dashboards, and bespoke rollback scripts. This creates inconsistent safety posture between product teams and slows rollouts.

Proposal: Ship a product-centric A/B framework (Experiment Controller) that combines: 1) declarative experiment manifests for model versions, 2) an adaptive exposure scheduler that ramps cohorts according to sequential statistical tests, 3) shadow/holdout support for dark-launch validations, and 4) automated rollback ("autorestore") triggered by preconfigured safety checks. The controller will expose both Console UI and REST/SDK primitives so infra, platform, and product teams can adopt it.

Key differentiators vs existing tooling: Focus on statistically-driven exposure (not only time-based ramps), built-in sequential tests (to control type I error in repeated checks), configurable Bayesian and frequentist gates, and explicit shadow-to-live promotion paths. Integrates with existing telemetry (Console metrics, traces) and runtime routing (Smart routing) so rollouts are consistent across hosted/dedicated/private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: Declarative experiment manifest supported via API and Console for creating A/B+shadow experiments
Exposure scheduler can run an adaptive ramp and pause/stop ramps based on configured statistical gates
Safety gates include at least: conversion delta, latency regression, error-rate increase, content-quality signal (from eval hooks)
Auto-rollback (autorestore) executes a safe revert path and creates audit entries & notification in Console when triggered
Experiment telemetry surfaces cohort-level metrics, sequential-test results, and sample-size guidance in the Console
SDK/REST endpoints return experiment status and allow programmatic hold/pause/force-rollback actions
tasks: Design experiment manifest schema (fields for cohort definitions, metrics, statistical plan, rollout plan)
Implement exposure scheduler prototype in runtime that can accept percent-based cohorts and deterministic hashing keys
Integrate sequential testing library (alpha spending / O'Brien-Fleming or Bayesian stopping rules) with metric ingestion pipeline
Console UI: experiment creation flow, live monitor with cohort breakdown and statistical diagnostics
Define default safety presets (low-risk consumer, high-risk enterprise) and guardrail templates
End-to-end tests: shadow traffic validation, rollback path testing, and observability retention checks
Docs: runbook for experimenters, API reference, and operational playbook for incident response
metrics: False positive rate for auto-rollback (target < 2% on default presets)
Percent of rollouts using adaptive exposure vs manual ramp
Mean time to recover from failed rollout (automated revert execution time)
Experiment success rate (meets lift objective without rollback)
statistical_checks: Support for sequential hypothesis testing with alpha spending; default alpha=0.05 with Pocock and O'Brien-Fleming options
Optional Bayesian posterior probability threshold (e.g., Pr(lift > 0) < 0.01 to trigger rollback)
Multiple-metric decision policy: configurable composition (AND/OR/weighted scoring) across primary and safety metrics
Minimum sample size enforcement per cohort before early-stop decisions (configurable per metric)
False discovery control when running multiple concurrent experiments (Benjamini-Hochberg FDR option)
Backfill-aware checks: support for delayed telemetry and replayed events in statistical calculations
exposure_plan: Cohort definitions: deterministic hashing on user_id/session_id with sticky assignment
Recommended ramp template: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with hold windows configurable (default 30 minutes)
Adaptive ramp: only advance when sequential-test p-value/confidence criteria met on primary metric(s)
Shadow mode support: copy production requests to new model without affecting live traffic for qualitative validation
Holdout windows: ability to keep a control cohort isolated for drift and calibration checks
Emergency kill-switch: global pause for experiment traffic with single-click in Console and REST call
rollback_triggers: Primary metric drop below configured minimum detectable effect threshold and statistical significance achieved
Latency p95 increases > X% (preset templates: 50% consumer, 25% enterprise)
Error rate increase above configured guardrail (absolute and relative thresholds)
Content-safety evals exceed violation threshold from eval webhook
Manual trigger by operator (Console or REST) or downstream dependency signals failure
open_questions: Which infra team will own the experiment controller runtime component for Private deployments? (eng ownership boundary)
Default metric telemetry window for comparison (30m, 1h, 6h?) — needs cross-team alignment with Observability
How should we present inconclusive tests in Console to avoid 'analysis paralysis' for PMs and engineers?
Do we expose Bayesian vs frequentist choice to end users or keep policy presets managed by Platform?
What retention period for experiment-level raw telemetry is required for audits and postmortems?
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-eager auto-rollback may revert benign variance. Mitigation: conservative default alpha and minimum sample size, and a 5-minute confirmation window before action.
Risk: Users misconfigure metrics and trigger false alarms. Mitigation: Console validation of metric definitions, pre-flight dry-run reports, and 'preview power' estimates.
Risk: Increased telemetry volume from shadow traffic. Mitigation: sampling knobs and lightweight validation-only shadow mode.
Risk: Divergent behavior in Private deployments due to slower telemetry pipelines. Mitigation: clear docs and a degraded-mode that recommends manual ramps in Private installs.
